rules.statement: A deed must be signed by the party making it, witnessed by a notary public and at least two other witnesses present simultaneously, and attested by both the notary public and witnesses.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) The essential elements of due execution of a deed as set out in section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance are (a) The deed must be signed by the party making it. (b) It must be signed in the presence of a licensed notary public and two or more witnesses. (c) The notary public and the witnesses must be present at the same time. (d) The execution of the deed must be duly attested by the notary. and the witnesses. The notary is as much an attesting witness as the two witnesses themselves. (2) Where the requirements of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance have been complied with the mere fact that the notary has inserted a false or wrong date of its execution does not render the deed void. 185 (3) The lapse of the notary may render him liable to be prosecuted for contravention of the provisions of the Notaries Ordinance. (4) The prohibition against alienation pending partition contained in s. 67(1) of the Partition Act applies only to a partition action which" is duty registered as a lis pendens under the Registration of Documents Ordinance (5) Where the purchase pending partition was by the plaintiff himself the plaintiff cannot be permitted to take advantage of his own wrongful act

rules.statement: The validity of a deed is not affected by a notary's insertion of an incorrect date provided the other requirements of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance are met.
